findings.title: Docstring still says "returns a list" after signature changed to return a dict
findings.body: The `evaluate` method's docstring reads "Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`" but the method now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. This will mislead anyone reading the docstring about the return type.

findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler cannot be instantiated — abstract methods not implemented
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` extends `StatefulDetectorHandler` but does not implement any of its abstract methods (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, `build_occurrence_and_event_data`). If `Detector.detector_handler` property is accessed for a detector with type `metric_alert_fire`, it will call `group_type.detector_handler(self)` (line 86 of `detector.py`), which attempts to instantiate the class and will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`. Even though the TODO comment acknowledges this is a placeholder, the class is registered as a `detector_handler` on `MetricAlertFire` and will crash at runtime if that code path is reached.

findings.title: Test passes wrong value (6 instead of 10) for group_2 occurrence, masking potential bugs
findings.body: In `test_state_results_multi_group`, the data packet sets `"group_2": 10`, but the expected occurrence is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 6, ...)`. The `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` helper ignores the `value` parameter entirely, so the test passes regardless. This means the test does not verify that the actual value from the data packet (10) is correctly forwarded to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. If a real implementation used the value (e.g., to include it in the occurrence), this test would not catch a mismatch.
